thread.title: Apple Stock Nicked By Slowing Services Growth | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Nicked By Slowing Services Growth | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) services business is forecast to decelerate next year, adding another worry to Apple stock heading into 2019.
X Macquarie Capital analyst Benjamin Schachter on Wednesday cut his price target on Apple stock to 188 from 222, but kept his outperform rating. He sees Apple services growth slowing to 21.8% in fiscal 2019 from 26% in fiscal 2018, which ended Sept. 29.
Apple stock rose 0.3% to 169.10 on the stock market today . Since hitting an all-time high of 233.47 on Oct. 3, Apple stock has tumbled 27.6% through Wednesday's close. Soft iPhone sales and the U.S.-China trade war have weighed on its shares.
"The three top drivers of Services over the past 3 years have been Licensing, App Store, and AppleCare," Schachter said in a report to clients. "We expect all three will slow in the coming quarters as tough comps and other issues impact growth rates."

Please contact customer service CLOSE App Store Commission Rates Threatened He added, "The smaller Services businesses — Music, iCloud, and Apple Pay — are not big enough to counter and pick up the slack to maintain current growth rates."
His growth projections do not include any change to App Store commissions. Schachter believes the 70/30 split of revenue between app creators and Apple will change, with Apple getting less than its current 30% cut.
"There hasn't been any movement on app commissions since competitive pressures drove the one-year+ subscription change from 30% to 15% in 2016, but we see regulatory, legal, and competitive pressures building on the app store model that may push a further decrease in commission," he said.
